artifacts.complete_sentence: === Equestrian statue ===. The equestrian statue of Marcus Aurelius in Rome is the only Roman equestrian statue which has survived into the modern period.
=== Ancient world ===. Hannibal caused great distress to many in Roman society.
=== Muslim world ===. Saladin has become a prominent figure in Muslim, Arab, Turkish and Kurdish culture, and he has been described as the most famous Kurd in history.

=== Early life (1571–1592) ===. Caravaggio (Michelangelo Merisi or Amerighi) was born in Milan, where his father, Fermo (Fermo Merixio), was a household administrator and architect-decorator to the marquess of Caravaggio, a town 35 km (22 mi) to the east of Milan and south of Bergamo. It was previously assumed that he had been born in Caravaggio.
=== Early life ===. Michael Faraday was born on 22 September 1791 in Newington Butts, Surrey, which is now part of the London Borough of Southwark. His family was not well off.
=== Reception ===. Although Verdi's operas brought him a popular following, not all contemporary critics approved of his work.

=== Recognition ===. In a survey of the 100 most prominent physicists conducted by Physics World, Maxwell was voted the third greatest physicist of all time, behind only Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein.

=== Family background ===. The Mahler family came from eastern Bohemia, now in the Czech Republic, and were of humble circumstances—the composer's grandmother had been a street pedlar. Bohemia was then part of the Austrian Empire; the Mahler family belonged to a German-speaking minority among Bohemians, and was also Jewish.

=== Power struggle ===. After Sun's death, Wang Jingwei became the first president of the Nationalist government, which soon fragmented into three competing factions: the center-right Nanjing government led by Chiang Kai-shek, the leftist Wuhan government led by Wang Jingwei, and the far-right Western Hills Group, originally convened in Beijing, which maintained its own Central Executive Committee in Shanghai.
=== South Africa ===. King's legacy includes influences on the Black Consciousness Movement and civil rights movement in South Africa.
=== Awards and honours ===. 1976: Rolling Stone magazine's "Band of the Year".

js_mismatches.json_val: Built Hadrian's Wall to mark the northern limit of Britannia and sponsored major Roman architectural works including the rebuilt Pantheon.
js_mismatches.js_val: Hadrian is important for the consolidation of the Roman Empire and for the physical landscape his building program left behind. His reign illustrates a shift from territorial expansion toward managing and defending an already vast imperial system.

js_mismatches.json_val: === Equestrian statue ===. The equestrian statue of Marcus Aurelius in Rome is the only Roman equestrian statue which has survived into the modern period.
js_mismatches.js_val: Combined Stoic philosophy with imperial rule during prolonged frontier wars, leaving the Meditations as a major work of ancient philosophy.

js_mismatches.json_val: === Ancient world ===. Hannibal caused great distress to many in Roman society.
js_mismatches.js_val: Carthaginian general and statesman who carried the Second Punic War into Italy and repeatedly defeated larger Roman armies before being defeated by Scipio at Zama.

js_mismatches.json_val: By 336, he had reoccupied most of the long-lost province of Dacia which Aurelian had been forced to abandon in 271.
js_mismatches.js_val: Roman emperor who reunited the empire and transformed imperial policy toward Christianity during the early fourth century.

js_mismatches.json_val: According to William of Tyre, although Nur ad-Din was "a mighty persecutor of the Christian name and faith," he was also "a just prince, valiant and wise, and according to the traditions of his race, a religious man." His sense of justice was never denied to anyone, regardless of their creed or origins. As a result of his justice, a Christian foreigner was said to have settled into Damascus, which was under Nur ad-Din's reign.
js_mismatches.js_val: Nur ad-Din left a lasting mark on military history through consolidation of Muslim Syria and the campaigns that preceded Saladin's rise.

js_mismatches.json_val: === Muslim world ===. Saladin has become a prominent figure in Muslim, Arab, Turkish and Kurdish culture, and he has been described as the most famous Kurd in history.
js_mismatches.js_val: Founder of the Ayyubid dynasty.

js_mismatches.json_val: Halted the westward expansion of the Mongol Empire at the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260, preserving Islamic civilization in Egypt and the Levant.
js_mismatches.js_val: Mamluk Sultan who defeated the Mongols.

js_mismatches.json_val: Consolidated French royal authority, reformed medieval judicial institutions, and was canonized as a Catholic saint in 1297.
js_mismatches.js_val: Strengthened French royal administration and personally led two crusades, becoming the only French king canonized in the Middle Ages.

js_mismatches.json_val: Published De revolutionibus orbium coelestium in 1543, triggering the Copernican Revolution and contributing fundamentally to the Scientific Revolution.
js_mismatches.js_val: Nicolaus Copernicus left a lasting mark on science through the heliocentric model presented in De revolutionibus.

js_mismatches.json_val: Revolutionized Western European painting through intense realism and a dramatic, high-contrast use of chiaroscuro and tenebrism, profoundly shaping the emergence of Baroque art.
js_mismatches.js_val: Caravaggio revolutionized European painting with stark chiaroscuro, naturalistic figures, and emotionally charged biblical scenes.

js_mismatches.json_val: Instrumental in developing classical chamber music, earning the epithets 'Father of the Symphony' and 'Father of the String Quartet'.
js_mismatches.js_val: Joseph Haydn left a lasting mark on music through his London Symphonies and string quartets.

js_mismatches.json_val: Goya is often referred to as the last of the Old Masters and the first of the moderns. Among the 20th-century painters influenced by Goya are the Spanish masters Pablo Picasso and Salvador Dalí who drew influence from Los caprichos and the Black Paintings of Goya.
js_mismatches.js_val: Goya bridged the Old Masters and modern art through court portraits, The Third of May 1808, and the dark imagery of the Black Paintings.

js_mismatches.json_val: Alex Ross writes "He not only left his mark on all subsequent composers but also molded entire institutions. The professional orchestra arose, in large measure, as a vehicle for the incessant performance of Beethoven's symphonies.
js_mismatches.js_val: Ludwig van Beethoven left a lasting mark on music through his Fifth and Ninth Symphonies.

js_mismatches.json_val: Critiqued 18th-century novels of sensibility through her fiction and formed part of the transition toward 19th-century literary realism.
js_mismatches.js_val: Jane Austen transformed the English novel through precise social observation, irony, and works such as Pride and Prejudice.

js_mismatches.json_val: Discovered electromagnetic induction, laws of electrolysis, and diamagnetism, laying the physical foundations for electromagnetic field theory and modern electrical power technology.
js_mismatches.js_val: Michael Faraday left a lasting mark on science through electromagnetic induction and the foundations of electric motor and generator technology.

js_mismatches.json_val: Formulated the philosophical doctrine of positivism and established sociology as a systematic science, seeking to create a scientific framework for social order following the French Revolution.
js_mismatches.js_val: Auguste Comte formulated positivism and argued that society could be studied systematically, helping establish sociology as a distinct field of inquiry.

js_mismatches.json_val: === Reception ===. Although Verdi's operas brought him a popular following, not all contemporary critics approved of his work.
js_mismatches.js_val: Giuseppe Verdi left a lasting mark on music through La traviata, Aida and Otello.

js_mismatches.json_val: Discovered the relationship between heat and mechanical work, establishing energy principles that led to the First Law of Thermodynamics.
js_mismatches.js_val: James Prescott Joule left a lasting mark on science through the mechanical equivalent of heat and the quantitative study of energy.

js_mismatches.json_val: Founded the American Red Cross and directed its humanitarian relief operations during wars and natural disasters for twenty-three years.
js_mismatches.js_val: Remembered for shaping historical developments in physician.

js_mismatches.json_val: === Recognition ===. In a survey of the 100 most prominent physicists conducted by Physics World, Maxwell was voted the third greatest physicist of all time, behind only Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein.
js_mismatches.js_val: James Clerk Maxwell left a lasting mark on science through Maxwell's equations and the electromagnetic theory of light.

js_mismatches.json_val: Formulated the Periodic Law and created a predictive periodic table of elements used to correct known properties and anticipate undiscovered elements.
js_mismatches.js_val: Dmitri Mendeleev left a lasting mark on science through the periodic table and prediction of undiscovered elements.

js_mismatches.json_val: Served as Grand Mufti of Egypt and a central figure of Islamic Modernism, reforming religious thought through rationalist interpretation.

js_mismatches.js_val: Emperor Meiji ruled during the transformation of Japan into a modern industrial and national state.

js_mismatches.json_val: Remembered as a leading figure of the 19th-century Aestheticism movement and a master of late Victorian theatrical comedy.
js_mismatches.js_val: Wilde became a major figure of aestheticism through witty drama, criticism, and The Picture of Dorian Gray.

js_mismatches.json_val: Exerted a profound and wide-ranging influence on succeeding generations of 20th-century classical composers.
js_mismatches.js_val: Gustav Mahler left a lasting mark on music through his large-scale symphonies and Das Lied von der Erde.
